definitions.explanation: To think about something again and possibly change one's mind or perspective on it.

definitions.gloss: to recall, to look back on, to reflect on
definitions.explanation: To bring past events or memories to mind and think about them again.

examples.japanese: よく{思|おも}い{返|かえ}してみた。
{冷静|れいせい}に{思|おも}い{返|かえ}せば、{彼|かれ}の{言|い}うことも{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: Thinking it over calmly, I can understand what he's saying.

examples.japanese: {今|いま}{思|おも}い{返|かえ}しても{恥|は}ずかしい。
examples.english: Even now when I recall it, I feel embarrassed.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}を{思|おも}い{返|かえ}す。
examples.english: To look back on one's student days.

examples.japanese: あの{日|ひ}のことを{思|おも}い{返|かえ}すと{涙|なみだ}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: When I recall that day, tears come to my eyes.

examples.japanese: {過去|かこ}を{思|おも}い{返|かえ}して{反省|はんせい}する。
examples.english: To reflect on the past and learn from one's mistakes.

notes:
{思|おも}い{返|かえ}す combines {思|おも}う (to think) with {返|かえ}す (to return), conveying the sense of returning to past thoughts or reconsidering.

Usage patterns:
- 〜を{思|おも}い{返|かえ}す (to recall/reconsider something)
- {今|いま}{思|おも}い{返|かえ}しても (even now when I think back)
- よく{思|おも}い{返|かえ}してみる (to think it over carefully)

Transitivity: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
Conjugation: {五段|ごだん} (godan/u-verb)

Related words:
- {思|おも}い{出|だ}す: to remember, recall (more spontaneous)
- {振|ふ}り{返|かえ}る: to look back on, reflect
- {考|かんが}え{直|なお}す: to reconsider, think again
